claims: Teradyne posted multiple senior M&A execution/strategic-planning roles in September 2026, indicating organizational investment in inorganic-growth execution capacity.
This is a weak signal, not proof of a pending transaction; it increases the value of reconciling current debt, repurchases and acquisition capacity in the existing TER packet.
risks: Hiring signals can precede no transaction and must not be treated as transaction evidence.
More active inorganic growth can raise integration and capital-allocation risk if balance-sheet capacity is misread.
unknowns: Whether any material transaction is pending; current acquisition budget and financing posture.

claims: Serve announced an August 17, 2026 Grubhub/Wonder rollout in Chicago, Los Angeles and Alexandria and described a network exceeding 2,000 robots and 4,000 restaurants.
The announcement is relevant to distribution breadth and utilization optionality, but it does not resolve revenue concentration, unit economics, runway or financing overhang.
risks: Company-origin rollout metrics can overstate economic significance absent revenue/utilization/unit-economics disclosure.
Additional platforms reduce single-channel narrative dependence but do not establish diversified revenue concentration.
unknowns: Revenue contribution by platform/customer; utilization economics; contract minimums/termination rights; contribution margin by deployment.
